A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GPT-attention causal-world-model research. All 11 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of a pretrained Othello GPT on 1,000 random legal sequences, including confidence–legality relationships and conditional-independence ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds original head-pruning results, an illustrated recovered graph, and training/test n-gram analyses.

M1.justification: The covariance construction, entropy-difference confidence score and recursive discovery procedure remain unchanged. v2's modified-ICD pseudocode documents the restriction to newly added edges already specified in v1 Algorithm 1. Head pruning is introduced as an experimental ablation.

E1.justification: Coverage remains Othello move sequences, legality and attention-derived structures, using the retained pretrained model and random legal-sequence evaluation. The new pruning and n-gram analyses do not introduce a distinct domain or task; held-out real-world sequences constitute a split within existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 5 adds reverse-order pruning of high-confidence heads as a comparator to pruning low-confidence heads. The four existing CI-conditioning variants remain unchanged. Voita et al. is cited for pruning motivation, not evaluated as another baseline.

E3.justification: The new pruning experiment pools 8,000 sequence/head scores, applies thresholds at the 10th–90th percentiles, skips heads without retraining, and compares normalized legality under opposite pruning orders. Appendix B adds a protocol comparing 2–6-gram frequencies using training, random-test and held-out real-world sequences.

E4.justification: v2 adds a head-removal intervention testing the functional importance of structural confidence, an Othello graph-recovery case study in Figure 1, and training/test distribution analysis in Appendix B. The original conditioning-set ablation is retained as Figure 4.

E5.justification: v1 already reports 95% confidence intervals and statistical significance for the CI ablation. v2 specifies that these intervals use an unpaired t-test. Neither version reports additional repeated runs or seeds establishing an increase in replication.

E6.justification: New results show that pruning low-confidence heads generally preserves legality better than reverse-order pruning, and that random test sequences have lower training n-gram match frequencies. Figure 1 adds a recovered four-move graph. The reported 95% overall accuracy, 88% after 15 moves, and original CI-ablation findings are retained.

T1.justification: The SCM assumptions, Markov/faithfulness definitions and covariance derivation are retained, with some material moved into Section 2. Appendix B newly states a finite-context conditional-dependence assumption in Equation 11 and defines its n-gram frequency estimator, constituting limited formal additions.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a causal interpretation of masked GPT attention, zero-shot causal structure recovery, and an association between structural confidence and legal generation. The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain these claims; the new experiments supply additional support.

C2.justification: v2 interprets pruning as evidence that high-confidence heads contribute to legal generation and connects the illustrated graph's relations to move-enabling conditions. The short-sequence memorization explanation remains, while v1's speculation about endgame memorization is omitted.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility details: partial-correlation/Fisher-z CI testing, alpha = 0.01, averaging across eight heads, common prefix trimming of the 1,000 sequences, and explicit restricted-ICD pseudocode. These are newly documented details, not demonstrated changes to existing settings. However, v1's Causality Lab package link is removed.

R1.justification: Voita et al. (2019) is newly cited to support pruning without retraining. Positioning relative to ABCD, BERT and prior Othello world-representation studies remains substantially unchanged; other reference changes mainly concern formatting and bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: The title, author list and wording are revised, while the main five-section narrative remains intact. Definitions, the covariance derivation and algorithm explanation move into the main text; appendices and references are reorganized. Some section cross-references become inaccurate.

P2.justification: The paper switches from single-column to two-column layout and adds Figures 1, 5 and 6 plus colored modified-ICD pseudocode. Existing plots are resized and rearranged: CI-ablation panels change from a 2-by-2 grid to one row, and the length-10 confidence plot loses its connecting line.

improvement.justification: v1 relies largely on confidence–legality associations. v2's head-pruning intervention tests whether the identified heads matter for generation, substantially strengthening this central evidence, while expanded CI/ICD details improve reproducibility. The removed package link and cross-reference errors are limited drawbacks. The intervention supports functional importance without establishing the correctness of every recovered causal relation.
